title: Peshwari Naan
subtitle: Sweet almond and coconut stuffed flatbread
excerpt: Naan bread filled with a fragrant paste of ground almonds, desiccated coconut, and a little sugar, then cooked in a very hot oven or under a hot grill until puffed and lightly charred. The sweet stuffed naan from British-Indian curry houses.

recipe.sourceNotes: Peshwari naan is a British-Indian restaurant creation, named after Peshawar in Pakistan. The stuffed naan with almonds, coconut, and sweetness was developed by British-Indian restaurants as a sweet accompaniment to curry, particularly popular alongside a mild tikka masala or korma. In Pakistan and Afghanistan, the naan of Peshawar is a large, plain flatbread baked in a tandoor, without any sweet filling. The British version is an original adaptation.

recipeTools.notes: Or a very hot baking tray under a grill.

content.text: The dough needs to be soft and pillowy, achieved with a combination of yoghurt and milk. Rest it for at least an hour so the gluten relaxes and the naan stretches without springing back. The filling should be moist enough to hold together but not so wet it bursts through the dough when rolled. Cook under a very hot grill or in a dry pan over maximum heat so the outside chars before the inside dries out.

Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Add the yoghurt, warm milk, and oil. Mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour until puffed.
Mix the ground almonds, coconut, and sugar with enough warm water (about 2 tablespoons) to make a paste that holds together.

Divide the dough into 4 balls. Flatten each ball, place a quarter of the filling in the centre, and gather the edges of the dough up around it. Pinch firmly to seal. Roll out each filled ball gently into an oval about 5 mm thick.

Cook in a very hot dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the surface is puffed and charred in spots, or place under a very hot grill for 2 to 3 minutes per side. Brush immediately with melted ghee before serving.
